**Claude finished @cmungall's task in 11m 2s** —— [View job](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/actions/runs/42364487042)

---
### Review — PR #6194 · Bacterial MCL PHA synthesis and mobilization

**Status: changes requested** ([review submitted](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/pull/6194))

- [x] Gather PR context (diff scope, module + family + gene reviews)
- [x] Load `aigr-pr-review` skill conventions
- [x] Check module YAML: boundaries, parts, evidence, actions
- [x] Verify PMIDs and verbatim supporting text
- [x] Check PANTHER family reviews (labels, representative members, verdicts)
- [x] Check validation status (CI "Build and test" ✅)
- [x] Post review + set PR review status

---

### Summary checklist

- [x] Schema validation passes — CI **Build and test** green ([run](https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/actions/runs/42364486964))
- [x] All PMIDs verified as real (spot-checked 10 against `publications/` cache)
- [x] Supporting text matches publication content (spot-checked 10 quotes verbatim, incl. ones spanning cache line wraps)
- [x] PANTHER family labels verbatim-correct against `interpro/panther/panther.obo` (all four)
- [ ] **Review actions well-justified** — see 🔴 and 🟡 below
- [ ] **GO terms correct and specific** — several core/annoton MFs sit at near-root genera
- [x] Core functions biologically accurate (the *biology* is right; *granularity* and *verdict strength* are the problems)
- [x] No over-annotation missed — the PhaZ glycerolipid/MAG-lipase propagations are correctly caught at gene level

The scientific content here is genuinely strong. Strain hygiene is the best I've seen in this repo: KT2442-vs-KT2440 provenance on `PMID:17170116`/`PMID:41055782`, GPo1 alias handling, the PhaG forward-vs-reverse direction distinction (`PMID:12200450` measures CoA→ACP, correctly not reversed anywhere), and the class I comonomer framing (`PMID:35341893`'s abstract really does cap 3HD at 1.2–2.1 mol%, and the reviews say "not predominantly medium-chain"). `CUPNH/phaC` GO:0042619 `ACCEPT` applies the participation test exactly right — PhaC catalyses the polyester-forming step itself.

My objections are about **verdict strength**, not facts.

---

### 🔴 CRITICAL — resolved family verdicts replaced by `UNRESOLVED`, deleting `member_exceptions` and `affected_subfamilies`

This PR overwrites two previously curated family reviews (`reviewed_by: claude-code`, 2026-11-02) and withdraws their resolved judgments. Net across both files: **4 `TOO_DEEP` → `UNRESOLVED`, 1 `SOUND` → `UNRESOLVED`, 1 `FAMILY_WIDE` → `UNRESOLVED`, 2 `SUBFAMILY_ONLY` → `UNRESOLVED`**, plus deletion of ≥4 `member_exceptions` entries and 3 `affected_subfamilies`/`applicable_subfamilies` lists. `interpro/panther/PTHR43194/PTHR43194-review.yaml` now has **9 assessments, all `UNRESOLVED`** — zero resolved verdicts, at `review_status: COMPLETE`.

The stated rationale misreads what `TOO_DEEP` asserts. Per `src/ai_gene_review/schema/family_review.yaml:805`:

> `TOO_DEEP`: The function arose later than the node it is placed at, so clades that never had it inherit the term.

That is a claim about **node placement**, not about catalytic loss in a member. But the new reasons withdraw it on a loss standard:

- `interpro/panther/PTHR43194/PTHR43194-review.yaml:148` (`PTN002455972`, GO:0009102 biotin biosynthetic process): *"neither its universal propagation nor categorical absence in PhaG follows… the prior TOO_DEEP verdict is withdrawn."* The prior verdict never claimed absence in PhaG — it named **SF3 RsbQ**, a σB stress-signalling protein, as a clade that cannot be in biotin synthesis. That observation is untouched by any PhaG uncertainty, and the `affected_subfamilies: [SF3]` record was deleted with it. Same at `:126` for GO:0090499.
- `interpro/panther/PTHR43798/PTHR43798-review.yaml:216` and `:239` (`PTN008685307`, GO:0047372 / GO:0046464): *"The previous absence-of-assay rationale did not establish a catalytic loss."* The previous rationale was that a 2-seed ABHD6 assertion sits on a 64-leaf node spanning SF33 fungal/Dictyostelium putative hydrolases and SF26. That is textbook `TOO_DEEP`.

The cascade is visible in the file itself. `PTHR43194-review.yaml:160` states the mechanism outright: *"its schema representation changes only because UNRESOLVED cannot carry member_exceptions… The current schema/semantic combination cannot preserve that independently negative member."* That is not a validator defect — `family_review.yaml:490` requires a `member_exception` to be **anchored in an adjudicated node** (`NEEDS_PRUNING`/`TOO_DEEP`/`WRONG_NODE`/`LOSS_SUPPORTED`) *by design*, "so an exception is always anchored in an adjudicated node rather than standing alone." Withdrawing the node verdict broke the anchor; the exceptions were then deleted to satisfy the constraint. The PR body's framing ("the production validator's inability to enforce a member exception under UNRESOLVED scope") inverts cause and effect.

It also contradicts this PR's own gene reviews. `genes/ECTOL/phaZ/phaZ-ai-review.yaml:53,81` marks GO:0046464 and GO:0047372 `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED` for P26495 — exactly the member exception `PTHR43798-review.yaml:272` now declines to record ("an invented PhaZ negative exception"). The same evidence yields opposite verdicts at gene and family level in one changeset.

**Ask:** restore `TOO_DEEP` on `PTN002455972` (GO:0009102, GO:0090499) and `PTN008685307` (GO:0047372, GO:0046464) with their `affected_subfamilies`; restore `SUBFAMILY_ONLY`/`FAMILY_WIDE` scopes and add P26495 (and keep Q88QE1 AcoC, O85207 PhaG) as `member_exceptions` rather than blanking the scope. The new PhaZ-in-SF5 finding is a *reason to add an exception*, not to withdraw the clade judgment.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=On%20branch%20cmungall%2Faigr-mcl-pha-taxon-audit%2C%20restore%20the%20resolved%20family%20verdicts%20that%20were%20downgraded%20to%20UNRESOLVED.%20In%20interpro%2Fpanther%2FPTHR43194%2FPTHR43194-review.yaml%20restore%20assessment%3A%20TOO_DEEP%20with%20affected_subfamilies%20%5BSF3%20RSBQ%5D%20on%20PTN002455972%20for%20GO%3A0009102%20(line%20148)%20and%20GO%3A0090499%20(line%20126)%2C%20restore%20scope%20FAMILY_WIDE%20with%20member_exceptions%20for%20Q88QE1%20and%20O85207%20on%20the%20GO%3A0016787%20term%20assessment%20(line%20160)%2C%20and%20restore%20SUBFAMILY_ONLY%20SF5%20on%20GO%3A0090499%20(line%20180).%20In%20interpro%2Fpanther%2FPTHR43798%2FPTHR43798-review.yaml%20restore%20TOO_DEEP%20with%20affected_subfamilies%20%5BSF33%2C%20SF26%5D%20on%20PTN008685307%20for%20GO%3A0047372%20(line%20216)%20and%20GO%3A0046464%20(line%20239)%2C%20and%20restore%20scope%20SUBFAMILY_ONLY%20SF5%20on%20the%20GO%3A0047372%20term%20assessment%20(line%20272)%20adding%20UniProtKB%3AP26495%20as%20a%20member_exception%20citing%20the%20MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED%20rows%20in%20genes%2FECTOL%2FphaZ%2FphaZ-ai-review.yaml.%20Use%20git%20show%20origin%2Fmain%20for%20the%20prior%20text.%20Rationale%3A%20TOO_DEEP%20asserts%20node%20placement%2C%20not%20catalytic%20loss%2C%20and%20family_review.yaml%20line%20490%20requires%20member_exceptions%20to%20be%20anchored%20in%20an%20adjudicated%20node%20by%20design.&repo=ai4curation/ai-gene-review)

---

### 🟡 IMPORTANT

**1. `PSEPK/phaZ` GO:0004806 `MODIFY` → `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE` overstates a surrogate-substrate activity, and drops the correct MF recommendation.**
`genes/PSEPK/phaZ/phaZ-ai-review.yaml:26`. The reason's own evidence is *"A very low but detectable activity was observed when the assay was developed overnight"* with *"longer tested triacylglycerols were undetectable"* — on tributyrin (C4), the standard esterase surrogate, from a **KT2442** enzyme, on an **IEA/TreeGrafter** row. Against the promiscuous-activity tiers in `projects/ENZYME_SPECIFICITY.md`, that is "real in vitro activity of unknown relevance" → `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED`, not "a genuine secondary activity" → `KEEP_AS_NON_CORE`. The C4-only-with-overnight-development profile is also specifically *not* triacylglycerol lipase chemistry; a carboxylesterase genus would be the honest term.

It is also framed inconsistently with its own paired row: GO:0046503 is `MODIFY`'d away at `:45` precisely because *"that in-vitro activity does not establish native glycerolipid catabolism."* Both rows derive from the same tributyrin number.

The knock-on matters more. The removed `MODIFY` was the only place the review recommended **GO:0050527**, the gene's actual molecular function. After this change `existing_annotations` contains one MF row (triacylglycerol lipase, kept) and no row — existing or `NEW` — asserting mcl-PHA depolymerase activity. `core_functions` still carries GO:0050527, but the actionable annotation recommendation is gone from a `status: COMPLETE` review of a characterised depolymerase.

**2. `PTHR36837` is marked `HETEROGENEOUS` with all four term scopes `UNRESOLVED`.**
`interpro/panther/PTHR36837/PTHR36837-review.yaml:8,58,74,86,102`. This is the canonical PhaC family — class I and class II enzymes catalyse the same reaction on the same fold with the same catalytic triad, differing in chain-length preference. That is `MOSTLY_COHERENT` ("Members share the function except for identified exceptions", `family_review.yaml:792`) with the SF4/Q8PAX3 branch as the named exception. Declaring `GO:0042621 poly(3-hydroxyalkanoate) biosynthetic process` `UNRESOLVED` for a family named *POLY(3-HYDROXYALKANOATE) POLYMERASE SUBUNIT PHAC* is the clearest `FAMILY_WIDE`/`SUBFAMILY_ONLY(SF5)` candidate in the PR. The stated bar — "activity of every member" (`:76`) — is one no family review can ever clear, so applying it makes `FAMILY_WIDE` unusable.

**3. The two PhaZ realizers get asymmetric MF granularity on equivalent evidence.**
Module `modules/bacterial_mcl_pha_synthesis_and_mobilization.yaml:496` gives the KT2440 realizer `GO:0050527 poly(3-hydroxyoctanoate) depolymerase activity`; `:568` gives the GPo1 realizer `GO:0016788 hydrolase activity, acting on ester bonds` — three steps from the root. `knowledge_gaps:682` justifies this by product-size resolution, but product size is equally unresolved for KT2442 (its abstract says only "endo/exo-mcl-PHA depolymerases"), while the **substrate** basis is if anything stronger for GPo1: `PMID:11133449` describes *native* primarily C8/C6 polymer, versus commercial C8/C6 polymer for the KT2442 enzyme. Either both take GO:0050527, or both use `proposed_molecular_function`.

Relatedly, `genes/ECTOL/phaZ/phaZ-ai-review.yaml:147` puts `GO:0016788` in `core_functions.molecular_function` while authoring a matching `proposed_new_terms` entry at `:154`. CLAUDE.md covers this case exactly: leave `molecular_function` unset and set `proposed_molecular_function` to the `proposed_name`. A near-root genus as the stated core function of a characterised depolymerase is uninformative.

**4. `ECTOL/phaZ` GO:0016020 membrane `UNDECIDED` where the review has already made the argument.**
`genes/ECTOL/phaZ/phaZ-ai-review.yaml:24`. The reason is correct and sufficient — "a PHA granule has a phospholipid monolayer" — and I confirmed P26495 has **zero** `TRANSMEM` features in `genes/ECTOL/phaZ/phaZ-uniprot.txt`. A single-seed TreeGrafter membrane IEA on a soluble intracellular hydrolase with no TM segment and a monolayer-bound substrate is `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED`. Note the sibling PTHR43798 review reaches the stronger verdict for the same term on the same node family (`TOO_DEEP` at `:123`, kept): "ABHD6 has a transmembrane anchor that the soluble bacterial members do not share."

**5. `PSEAE/phaG` leaves both BioH IBA rows `UNDECIDED` without running the comparator check.**
`genes/PSEAE/phaG/phaG-ai-review.yaml:25,61`. The IBA reading is done properly — `PTN002455972`, BioH P13001 seed, SF5 placement, no IRD/IKR — and `pseae-consultation/evidence.md` records that no biotin-specific PAO1 test was found. But one check settles it and was not run: **does PAO1 encode its own `bioH` ortholog, and is the `phaG` disruption mutant a biotin prototroph?** `PMID:10713430`'s mutant grew on both gluconate and fatty acids (40% / wild-type PHA), which is hard to reconcile with it being the sole pimeloyl-ACP methyl esterase. If PAO1 has a dedicated BioH, GO:0090499 and GO:0009102 are over-propagation and should be `MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED`. Leaving a chemistry-specific term like GO:0090499 unadjudicated in a `status: COMPLETE` review needs that check first, or an explicit statement of why it fails.

---

### 🔵 SUGGESTIONS

- **`PSEAE/phaG` GO:0016747 `NEW` uses `evidence_type: IC`** (`:90`). IC means inferred by a curator from *another GO annotation of the same gene product*. The actual basis is (a) `PMID:10713430`'s own conclusion for *P. aeruginosa* PhaG and (b) purified biochemistry on the *P. putida* ortholog — i.e. `IMP` or `ISS` (with `UniProtKB:O85207`), not `IC`.
- **A limitation quote is used as function support.** `genes/PSEPK/phaG/phaG-ai-review.yaml:166` cites *"no in vitro data on acyl-ACPs, the substrate in the forward direction is available"* in `core_functions.supported_by`. That sentence supports the caveat, not the activity. Keep it in `description`/`suggested_questions` and drop it from `supported_by`.
- **Upstream EC error worth a `source_defects` entry.** `genes/PSEAE/phaG/phaG-uniprot.txt:7` has `DE EC=2.4.1.-` on `(R)-3-hydroxydecanoyl-ACP:CoA transacylase`. EC 2.4 is glycosyltransferases; an acyl transfer is EC 2.3.1.-. Given how carefully this PR tracks provenance, that is a free `WRONG_*` defect against UniProt.
- **`proposed_parent` too high.** `genes/PSEPK/phaZ/phaZ-ai-review.yaml:222` parents the proposed mcl-PHA depolymerase term on `GO:0016787 hydrolase activity` (the branch root). `GO:0016788`, or the actual parent of GO:0050527, would place it correctly. The `ECTOL/phaZ` version (`:161`) already uses GO:0016788.
- **Run `just backfill-record-sections genes/ECTOL/phaZ`.** The UniProt quote at `:31` has no `record_section`, where `PSEAE/phaG` and `CUPNH/phaC` do.
- **`CUPNH/phaC` GO:0005737 → GO:0070088** (`:26`) is fine by the house rule, but the cited paper also shows PhaC *detaching* from aged granules (`:117`), so there is a real cytoplasmic pool. `ACCEPT` cytoplasm + `NEW` granule (IDA) would lose less. Not blocking.
- **Second-hand quoting.** Several `supported_by` entries quote `analysis/.../primary-scope.md` quoting a paper (e.g. `PSEPK/phaZ:34`). Legal under the `file:` rules, and the externally-read-full-text situation is documented, but it means the quote can't be checked against the publication. Worth a line in the gene notes saying so.

---

### Verdict

Requesting changes, driven almost entirely by the 🔴. The biology, strain discipline and quote hygiene in this PR are above the repo's bar; what blocks it is that it **removes** correct, well-evidenced curation from two previously reviewed PANTHER families and leaves them with no resolved verdicts, on a reading of `TOO_DEEP` the schema does not support — then deletes the `member_exceptions` the schema was designed to carry. Restoring those verdicts and recording P26495 as an exception (rather than blanking the scope) would resolve it; items 1–5 above are the remaining substantive asks.

*Note: `just`/`uv` are not installed on this runner, so I relied on the green CI "Build and test" run for schema validation rather than running `just validate-all` locally. Quote and PANTHER-label checks above were done by hand against the cached publications and `panther.obo`.*
